comentarios.texto: This test only asserts that a message is absent, so it would still pass if `--features=rolling-updates` were not honoured and the command stopped with the feature-disabled error. Add a positive assertion that the metadata command actually ran, such as `assertMessage("Metadata:")` or an exit-code check of 0.

hist.text: UpdateCommandDistTest.java:58-62 testMissingOptionOnSave only does assertNoMessage("Missing required argument"), so it would also pass if the feature gate rejected the command. The PR changed this launch line to add ENABLE_FEATURE, but testCompatible (line 71-75) already asserts "Metadata:" and exit code 0 with the flag, so the feature path is covered elsewhere; this is a weak-assertion tidy-up.

The PR changes UpdateCommandDistTest.java:59 to enable rolling-updates, but line 61 only checks for absent output; CLIResult.java:92-94 checks neither errors nor exit status. UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-49 exits early when the feature is disabled, and CLITestExtension.java:112-114,149-155 performs no automatic exit-code assertion for distribution tests, so that failure would still pass this test.

Keep TP nit. The absence-only assertion is not new: the PR only appends ENABLE_FEATURE to the @Launch at UpdateCommandDistTest.java:59; `cliResult.assertNoMessage("Missing required argument")` (:61) was already the whole test, and it still checks what it was written for (output option is optional on save). The feature-gate path the comment worries about is verified elsewhere in the same PR: :73-74 `result.assertMessage("Metadata:"); assertEquals(0, result.exitCode());` with ENABLE_FEATURE, plus the new testFeatureNotEnabled asserting the disabled error. Adding a positive assertion here is test tidying.

I retain TP: the changed launch exercises the newly gated command, but assertNoMessage checks only stdout, and the distribution extension does not assert successful exit. The new feature-disabled branch returns an error without that stdout message, so this test passes without executing metadata generation. testCompatible supplies --file and therefore does not verify successful execution with the output option omitted. Although the weak assertion predates this PR, the PR changes this test’s invocation and introduces the early-return path it fails to detect; this is a behavioral test gap, not merely tidying.
